title: How to Improve Your Agents: Academic Lit Review
talk_summary: An academic literature review of agent-improvement methods: self-refine/reflection loops, test-time compute scaling via MCTS with contrastive reflection and multi-agent debate verifiers, and distilling search traces into smaller models.

takeaways.what_they_do: A small/cheap model generates its own critique, then a large model edits that critique to be compatible with the small model's reasoning style before the small model revises; iterated until correct.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're actually using large language model to edit the smaller models feedback so that it's more tailored towards the smaller model
takeaways.numbers: 48% after three feedback/edit iterations, beating supervised training data on BigBench-hard style tasks

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of one prompt judging whether an action/state is good, ask models to argue both for and against, counterbalancing single-model bias in the value estimate.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we find this evaluation process can be much more robust if we use in a form of a debate
takeaways.numbers: Best non-trained method on OSWorld; #1 on VisualWebArena leaderboard

takeaways.technique: Contrastive reflection cached in vector DB
takeaways.what_they_do: After each task, the agent writes a contrastive reflection (what worked vs. what failed) into a vector store; future tasks retrieve similar reflections to bias decisions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: save this experience to a vector database ... during any future task the agent will also retrieve reflection similar to the current task

takeaways.technique: Exploratory (backtrack) traces instead of imitation of best action
takeaways.what_they_do: Train/condition on the full search-tree traversal — including failed actions and backtracks — rather than only the final good action, so the model learns to explore and recover.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the models will learn how do you actually linearize the search tree traversal to motivate the model to learn how to explore backtrack and evaluate
takeaways.numbers: Exploratory learning outperforms imitation learning under constrained test-time budget

takeaways.technique: Test-time compute scaling as substitute for bigger model
takeaways.what_they_do: Keep the base model fixed and spend more inference steps (reflection iterations, search) to raise task success, rather than routing to a stronger model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: instead of pre-training a large language model you take the model as it is but give it more steps or budgets in terms of inference
takeaways.numbers: Performance increases roughly linearly with inference budget

takeaways.what_they_do: Flags that multi-user/multi-agent settings need scheduling, DB side-effect avoidance, and human-handover policies, not just single-task benchmarks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we will encounter all these kind of system level problems about scheduling how do we interact with database to avoid side effects
